takeaway: Dry season holds. Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) has a clear, breezy Monday on the North Pacific. Nicoya reaches about 35°C, a bit less hot than Sunday because the trade winds are back to moderate. No rain is expected here. For surf, the Caribbean trades stay offshore at Nosara. They hold through Tuesday, ease Tuesday night and Wednesday, then come back stronger Thursday night and Friday. Dawn to late morning is the best window every day. No rainy spell and no tropical storm threat for the next two weeks.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Mon Nov 23 – Wed Nov 25)
periods.pattern: IMN calls today clear and windy early, then clear to a few clouds, with moderate trades over Guanacaste that ease in the afternoons. The air is dry, so skies stay clear and it stays hot. Only the mountains of the Central and South Pacific get scattered afternoon showers. The Papagayo gap winds keep blowing from the northeast and east today and Tuesday, then go light Tuesday night. For a few hours that night a light south to southeast breeze is possible before the wind turns north again on Wednesday. Every model and ensemble average keeps Nicoya at a trace of rain or less.
periods.implications: Sunny and hot: about 35°C inland at Nicoya, low 30s at the beach, about 23°C at night. Breezy and a bit less sticky today and Tuesday. Wednesday is the calmest and muggiest day. Great for outdoor plans. Bring sun protection and water, not rain gear.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Thu Nov 26 – Sun Nov 29)
periods.pattern: A strong north wind surge reaches the Gulf of Mexico midweek, and the trades build hard behind it. The marine forecast has northeast to east winds of 15–20 knots in the Papagayo area Thursday and 20–25 knots Thursday night and Friday, a notch stronger than yesterday's call. All three ensemble averages and both main models show a strong east wind stream across Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica Thursday night into the weekend. The extra wind pushes rain onto the Caribbean side: the European and AI ensemble averages show about 0.5–1 inch on Costa Rica's Caribbean coast in the 24 hours ending Friday evening, the US ensemble average about half an inch. Nicoya stays at a trace.
periods.implications: Windy, dusty and a little less hot from Thursday night through the weekend. Boat and paddle trips get rough on the windiest days, Friday especially. Tie down loose gear and be careful with fire. Rain at the beach is very unlikely.
periods.confidence: High on dry. Moderate-high on how strong the Friday wind gets.

periods.label: Days 8–15 (Mon Nov 30 – Mon Dec 7)
periods.pattern: A classic dry-season trade-wind pattern. The ensemble averages keep a steady east wind stream across Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica through about Dec 3, a little weaker around Dec 5, then building again toward Dec 7. The European ensemble average again shows a weak low off southern Costa Rica and Panama around Nov 29 and Dec 3. That's the usual low that forms downwind of the mountains when the trades blow hard, not a storm. The heavier rain on the maps stays well offshore to the south and on the Caribbean side. IMN's sub-seasonal outlook has the North Pacific at 0–50 mm a week for Nov 23–29 and Nov 30–Dec 6, says the dry season is now set across the whole Pacific side, and keeps rain below normal into mid-December with a low chance of extreme rain.
periods.implications: Plan freely. Expect sunny, windy, dusty days and warm, breezy nights. The calmer days for boat trips look like the stretch around Dec 4–5, but that's a rough guess this far out.
periods.confidence: High on dry. Moderate on day-to-day wind strength.

surfWinds.regime: Caribbean trade winds (northeast to east), offshore at Nosara, for the whole period. Steady today and Tuesday, a short lull Tuesday night and Wednesday, then stronger from Thursday night. No Pacific onshore pattern in sight, apart from a few hours of light south-southeast breeze possible Tuesday night.
surfWinds.detail: The Papagayo marine forecast (issued about 3 a.m. Costa Rica time) has northeast to east winds of 15–20 knots today, tonight and Tuesday. Tuesday night it goes light, around 10 knots from the southeast to south, then turns northwest to north late. Wednesday it's north to northeast at 10–15 knots, then northeast at 15–20 knots offshore Wednesday night. It builds to 15–20 knots Thursday and 20–25 knots Thursday night and Friday. Off Nicoya and to the south, winds stay light and variable (under 5 knots), so the offshore breeze reaches Nosara over the land, not along the coast. IMN says the trades ease in the afternoons, so expect the sea breeze to turn it side-on after midday. Swell (open-ocean numbers, not beach heights): south to southwest 6–8 ft at 15 seconds today, then a longer-period pulse, 4–7 ft at 17–18 seconds, Tuesday and Wednesday. By Thursday it's 6–9 ft with a shorter period (12 seconds). Nicaragua should be offshore all day today, Tuesday, and again from Thursday. That points to clean Nosara mornings, but not all-day offshore here.
surfWinds.bestWindows: Today and Tuesday: dawn to late morning. Wednesday: dawn to mid-morning. The offshore is lighter and less reliable after the Tuesday-night lull, and the sea breeze comes earlier. Thursday Nov 26 to about Dec 3: dawn to late morning. On the windiest days (Friday) the offshore may hold past noon but will be strong and gusty.
surfWinds.confidence: High on offshore mornings. Moderate on Wednesday morning and on the afternoon sea-breeze timing.

gyreWatch.status: Not established. No watch needed. No prolonged rainy spell expected.
gyreWatch.possibleTiming: Nothing organized through about Dec 7. The US hurricane center expects no tropical storm formation in the eastern Pacific in the next 7 days. The global tropics outlook (issued Nov 17, not yet updated) gives only a small chance of an eastern Pacific storm in late November or early December.
gyreWatch.supporting: Nothing meaningful. The only low on the maps is the weak low off southern Costa Rica and Panama that forms when the trades blow hard.
gyreWatch.conflicting: Strong trades, low pressure staying well to the south, and El Niño all favor drier than normal weather. The tropics outlook and IMN both favor below-normal rain for Central America.

whatChanged: The trades are back to moderate today, so Monday is a touch less hot than Sunday (Nicoya about 35°C vs 37°C). The Papagayo offshore now holds at 15–20 knots through Tuesday instead of easing; the lull shrinks to Tuesday night and Wednesday. The return surge is stronger: 20–25 knots Thursday night and Friday, up from 15–20. Swell is a bit bigger today (6–8 ft), with a longer-period pulse Tuesday and Wednesday. Still dry, still no storms.
practical: Surf dawn to late morning today and Tuesday, and go extra early Wednesday. Wednesday is the best boat or paddle day. Expect strong wind and dust Thursday night through the weekend, with rough water Friday. Plan outdoor events freely through early December. Stay hydrated and avoid open burning.
